proposals.evidence: Andersen calls aṁta plural 'borderers; neighbors' and compares RV ánta, Pali anta. Turner 347 has the boundary/proximity noun and Prakrit aṁta; the human plural reflects a straightforward boundary-dweller sense, though Turner does not list this precise Ashokan use.
